inputs.original_text: This is bigger than one conviction. France’s new “psychological subjection” law gives authorities a convenient, elastic label they can use against communities they want to bring into line. Father Bernard Domini, the abbot who leads the Missionary Family of Notre-Dame, is being made an example—and the public is being asked to accept it as protection. That’s how control gets normalized: officials define which beliefs are dangerous, then use vague language to make dissent look like a threat. Today it’s this community; the precedent can be turned on anyone inconvenient.
